image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of an African crocodile (Nile crocodile) resting on a sandy bank. The image focuses primarily on the head and upper torso. The mouth is slightly open, revealing conical teeth. The skin texture is highly detailed, showing rough, bony scutes on the dorsal side and smoother, lighter scales on the ventral jaw area. The eye is visible with a vertical slit pupil. There is some text/watermark in the bottom left corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers to a distinct point, consistent with the V-shape of a crocodile rather than the U-shape of an alligator. The head structure appears anatomically correct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is slightly agape, clearly showing large, conical, irregularly spaced teeth typical of crocodilians. The fourth lower tooth appears to fit into the upper jaw notch.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is positioned on top of the skull. A clear vertical slit pupil is visible. The surrounding tissue suggests the presence of eyelids/membranes, though the nictitating membrane itself isn't actively covering the eye.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The nostrils are clearly visible at the very end of the snout, appearing as raised openings.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows heavy armor plating (scutes) and extends out of frame, implying an elongated form.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal skin exhibits a complex pattern of raised, bony plates (scutes) that appear to follow longitudinal alignment, characteristic of Nile crocodiles.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of greys and browns with significant mud/dirt, and the texture is visibly rough and knobby.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside of the jaw and neck area shows significantly smoother, lighter-colored (whitish/grey) scales compared to the dorsal armor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The limbs are completely occluded by the body angle and the framing of the shot; only the head and back are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is not visible in this close-up crop of the head and shoulders.

artifact_observations.reasoning: There is faint, illegible white text or a watermark in the bottom left corner. It looks like AI-generated gibberish or a degraded stock photo watermark. It does not disrupt the main subject but is a noticeable artifact.

Slight softness/bleeding where the lower jaw meets the sand. The edge definition is slightly less sharp than the rest of the high-frequency skin texture, suggesting minor generation blur or focus issues.
